record.field: A workstation reports to several Odoo databases, each a local instance of the extension or a remote one given by URL and database, with its own enrollment and token

Destinations are the GSettings key inventory-destinations, read by parseDestinations of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory.js; erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-service.js keeps one queue, state file and keyring token per destination, and erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-prefs.js adds a destination by URL and database or from an instance of the extension.
The extension calls Odoo over HTTPS, and over plain HTTP only to this machine: 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 or localhost
urlAllowed of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory.js holds the policy; the service never calls a refused destination and the preferences explain the refusal before storing anything.
The workstation token lives in the GNOME keyring, bound to the URL and database it serves; the API key or the password serves the enrollment only and is never kept

erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/secret-store.js stores the token under the schema ca.technolibre.erplibre-home.inventory with the attributes destination, url and db; erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-prefs.js sends the key or the password once, in the enroll body, then empties the entries.
An employee gets a pairing code in Odoo from Stream Deck › My workstations › Add a workstation

The list header button of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/views/streamdeck_workstation_views.xml runs a server action that opens the wizard of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/wizard/streamdeck_pairing_wizard.py, which draws a fresh code for the current user.
A workstation enrolls by pairing code, by the employee's API key, or by login and password

streamdeck.service.enroll in ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py checks each method without opening a session; a password is refused when the account allows RPC by API key only. The preferences page builds the body of the chosen method.

Odoo sees of a workstation its host name (the default name, renamable), GNOME Shell, extension and contract versions, ERPLibre branch and commit, deck program, deck service state, and system name and version

The report state fills streamdeck.workstation; collectFacts of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-service.js reads /etc/os-release, the checkout and the deck settings. A report never renames a workstation.
Odoo sees of each deck its model, serial number, whether it is connected and since when, when it was last seen, and its firmware when readable

streamdeck.device in ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_device.py names the model from the USB product id (USB_MODELS); the report sets connected, connected_since and last_seen, and a null firmware keeps the stored one.
Archiving an employee revokes the tokens and archives the workstations; workstations, decks and history stay visible to the manager

res.users.write in ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/res_users.py archives the workstations of a user set inactive, and archiving a workstation clears its token hash; a token of an inactive employee is refused 403 user_inactive.

A lent deck follows its current workstation; an employee whose workstation had it keeps reading the deck and all its events, those of the holder included, never the holder's workstation nor its other decks

The record rules of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/security/streamdeck_rules.xml open a device to the employees whose workstation holds it or has an event of it, and its events with it; the report moves a deck to the workstation that declares it.
An ERPLibre runner runs the tests of an Odoo module on a throwaway database and sends each test's verdict to the registry as a Python test

erplibre:script/test/odoo_test_report.py --modules <a,b> reads each test from Odoo's log, references it as odoo.addons.<module>.tests.<file>.<Class>.<method>, drops its database, and pushes through Registre.pousser_verdicts of erplibre:script/test/requirement_report.py.
Offline, the extension keeps the dated events in a bounded local queue and sends them when Odoo answers again; the history carries the real time of each event

EventQueue of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory.js, saved in the destination's state file, leaves only what Odoo accepted; Odoo stores each event at its own time, and an event more than 5 minutes ahead of the reception at the reception time.
The extension shows an Odoo inventory page in its preferences (destinations, enrollment, detailed status) and a status line in the deck menu of the panel

_buildInventoryPage of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:prefs.js, on the model of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-prefs.js; the deck indicator erplibre-home-gnome-extension:indicators/device.js shows inventorySummary of the service.
The requirements of the inventory live in the registry, domain Inventory, each done one with the tests that prove it
data/requirement_inventory.xml of this module; its test checks that every proof names a test that exists, under the reference its runner pushes.
The history enters the inventory now: Odoo records a deck plugged, a deck unplugged and a change of the deck service state

streamdeck.event in ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_event.py, kinds plugged, unplugged and service_changed; the extension makes them with diffDecks and serviceChanged of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory.js.

Events are born on the workstation, dated and with a unique id, and Odoo keeps each id once; the full state sent with them sets the current inventory, and Odoo never infers an event from a state change

_store_events of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py acknowledges a known uuid again without change; _apply_decks disconnects the decks the state no longer lists without creating an event.
A workstation is identified by an HMAC-SHA256 of /etc/machine-id keyed by the Linux user and the destination's URL and database: two Odoo cannot match it, the raw id never leaves it

workstationFingerprint of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory.js; Odoo keeps one workstation per employee and fingerprint, and a re-enrollment of the same fingerprint keeps the record. A reinstalled machine (new machine-id) is a new workstation.
The workstation token is 32 random bytes returned once at enrollment; Odoo keeps only its SHA-256, which no employee reads, and the employee or the manager revokes it from the workstation

token_hash of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_workstation.py is restricted to the settings group; action_revoke_token clears it after a write check on the workstation; unenroll revokes it from the workstation itself.
A pairing code has 8 characters without ambiguity (no 0/O, 1/I), works for 10 minutes, once, for the employee who asked for it, and only that employee reads it

new_pairing_code of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py; the wizard's global rule shows a code to its creator only; repeated failures from one address are put on Odoo's login cooldown.
The workstation reports every 15 minutes and at each change, each call bounded by 10 seconds, never two reports at once to one destination

erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-service.js holds one report in flight per destination and follows Odoo's heartbeat_s; erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/odoo-http.js bounds the Soup session by TIMEOUT_S.
The offline queue holds at most 1000 events or 30 days per destination, the oldest dropped first; every report carries the running total of lost events, and Odoo keeps the largest

EventQueue of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory.js counts what its bound or its age drops; lost_events_total of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_workstation.py is the maximum received, so a replayed report changes nothing.
Each call carries its protocol version MAJOR.MINOR (1.0): Odoo refuses an unknown MAJOR with a code the extension shows, and accepts a newer MINOR, ignoring the keys it does not know

The protocol check of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py answers 400 protocol_unsupported; messageFor of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-prefs.js gives that code its own sentence.
A background part of the extension detects the decks, by GUdev events or else an asynchronous poll every 10 seconds, whether the deck indicator is shown or not; the indicator reads that same part

UsbWatch of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/usb-watch.js, started by the InventoryService that extension.js creates at enable; erplibre-home-gnome-extension:indicators/device.js reads its decks() and runs no lsusb of its own. An event takes the time it is observed.

A deck without a readable serial (sysfs serial first, lsusb next) is inventoried without a serial, owned by its workstation through the key workstation, USB product id and USB port, never merged with another workstation's deck

_deck_key of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py builds nosn:<workstation>:<product>:<port>; the extension reads sysfs serial before lsusb. A serial forged in that form is SD-INV-R44.
Holds only once SD-INV-R44 is done: until a serial is kept apart from the nosn: form, the key of a deck without serial is not reserved to its workstation.
The ERPLibre-extension contract moves to 1.2, a MINOR version; CONTRACT.md of the extension and the README of erplibre_streamdeck describe the report

erplibre-home-gnome-extension:CONTRACT.md 1.2, section Odoo inventory; erplibre:script/gnome-extension/erplibre_home_contract holds 1.2; ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/README.base.md, section on the wire protocol.

Odoo serves the JSON routes enroll, report and unenroll under /streamdeck/v1/, POST only; report and unenroll authenticate by the workstation token, and a malformed body is 400 bad_request with nothing written
ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/controllers/main.py calls streamdeck.service in sudo on a read-write cursor; the service validates a body whole before writing.
A revoked token, or the token of an archived employee or of an account that is not a Stream Deck user, is refused with a code the extension shows as enrollment revoked
The service answers 401 token_invalid or 403 user_inactive; erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-service.js then marks the destination revoked and sends that token no more.
A Stream Deck user reads and renames their workstations and revokes their tokens, reads the decks their workstations have had and the events of their workstations and of those decks

The access rights of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/security/ir.model.access.csv and the user rules of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/security/streamdeck_rules.xml; streamdeck.workstation.write lets an employee change the name only.
The Stream Deck manager reads every workstation, deck and event, revokes tokens and archives workstations

The manager rules of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/security/streamdeck_rules.xml; streamdeck.workstation.write lets the manager change the name and the active flag only, and only the manager's views show that flag.
Nobody writes the inventory by hand: only the routes write it, in sudo, bound to the workstation of the token

No group may create or delete a workstation, deck or event; the write guard of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_workstation.py refuses every other field outside sudo, and the service writes on the workstation its token names.
Menus: Stream Deck › My workstations (with Add a workstation) and My decks for every Stream Deck user, Stream Deck › Fleet (workstations, decks, events) for the manager
ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/views/streamdeck_menus.xml; the My actions carry the domain of the employee's own rule, so the manager also sees only their own there.
The inventory is translated into Canadian French in Odoo and in French in the extension, and the module's README is bilingual

ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/i18n/fr_CA.po and the template exported by Odoo; erplibre-home-gnome-extension:po/fr.po for the extension; README.base.md generates README.md and README.fr.md.
A failed report is silent apart from the status the extension shows: no notification, no log line
postJson of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/odoo-http.js never rejects and never logs; captureOutput of lib/spawn.js spawns without a log line; the service turns every failure into a status.
The pure logic of the inventory (payload, queue, URL policy, fingerprint, change detection) lives in lib/inventory.js under node --test; the rest has its manual checklist
erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory.js imports no gi module; erplibre-home-gnome-extension:test/manual.md, section Odoo inventory, lists the checks on a real session.
The Odoo test runner keeps the guarantees of requirement_report.py: nothing without the ERPLIBRE_REQUIREMENT_* variables, key never sent to Odoo nor shown, HTTPS or loopback, exit code of the tests

erplibre:script/test/odoo_test_report.py runs Odoo without the registry variables and on its own generated configuration, and pushes through the Registre of erplibre:script/test/requirement_report.py.
Non-goal: activities, the silent workstation and Settings › Stream Deck
Non-goal of the inventory: activities, the detection of a workstation that stops reporting and the Settings › Stream Deck page come with the next lot.
Non-goal: any configuration pushed from Odoo to the workstation
Non-goal of the inventory: Odoo never opens a connection to the workstation; driving the workstation comes with a later lot.
Non-goal: reading the firmware while the deck service holds the device
Non-goal of the inventory: the firmware stays empty rather than disputing the device with the deck service; a report without firmware keeps the one Odoo already has.
Non-goal: a client other than the GNOME extension
Non-goal of the inventory: the GNOME extension ERPLibre Home is the only client of the routes; the wire contract does not forbid another one.
Anti-goal: a secret in clear on the workstation, in its settings or in a log

The token lives in the keyring only; the state file and GSettings carry no secret, the user part of a URL is stripped before it is stored, and neither the extension nor the Odoo routes log a token, a key or a password.
Anti-goal: an employee who sees another employee's workstation; the only exception is the record of a deck their workstation had, and its events, read only

The user rules of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/security/streamdeck_rules.xml; the deck views show the workstation and employee names snapshot on each event, never a link to the other workstation; a pairing code is read by its creator only.
Holds only once SD-INV-R44 is done: until a serial is kept apart from the nosn: form, a workstation can make another workstation's deck without serial one it had, and read it with its events.
Anti-goal: an extension that slows GNOME Shell down when Odoo is slow or absent

Every call and every reading of the inventory path is asynchronous and cut at TIMEOUT_S, a cancelled process is killed, and stop() cancels calls and timers; GNOME Shell itself is checked on the manual checklist.
Anti-goal: identifying data in the code, the demo data, the comments or the commits

Examples are invented (example.invalid, 192.0.2.x, SN-INVENTED); erplibre:script/analyse/check_comment_hygiene.py reports identifying data in comments, and the commit-msg hook of erplibre:script/git/hooks refuses an address, an email or an account path in a commit body.
No test sweeps the files of the inventory: check_comment_hygiene.py runs by hand and from the pre-commit hook, which lists its findings without blocking the commit.
A deck declared by another workstation moves to it without confirmation, with a changed-workstation event that keeps the former and the new workstation
_apply_decks of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py moves the deck to the reporting workstation without confirmation.
No event records the move: streamdeck.event has no changed-workstation kind holding the former and the new workstation, and the move leaves no trace in the history.
Deck keys sn:<serial> and nosn:<workstation>:<product>:<port> cannot collide, and a serial outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} is refused 400 bad_request
_deck_key of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py keys a deck without serial as nosn:<workstation>:<product>:<port>.

The key of a deck with a serial is the bare serial, and a serial is any text up to 256 characters: a workstation that declares a serial of the form nosn:<workstation>:<product>:<port> takes over another workstation's deck without serial, with its history. Neither the sn: prefix nor the serial pattern is in the service, and no test pins them.
